outcome: Placental injury (reflecting hypoxia and uteroplacental insufficiency)
Maternal vascular malperfusion (e.g., increased syncytial knots, fibrinoid necrosis, focal perivillous fibrin depositions)
cohort: Pregnant women with COVID-19 who delivered between May 2020 and May 2021, compared to controls of non-infected women.
finding: The most common pathological findings in placentas of COVID-19 infected females were signs of maternal and fetal malperfusion, including increased decidual arteriopathy, placental injury, and features like syncytial knots, fibrinoid necrosis, and villitis.
